venue_now: Not shown in the text. The May entry (Text Summarization Branches Out, Barcelona, ACL, 2004, pp. 74-81) agrees with the 8-page file fetched from ACL Anthology W04-1013 (MANIFEST.json) and with papers.json.
what_it_is: Chin-Yew Lin's paper introducing the ROUGE package for automatic evaluation of summaries: ROUGE-N (n-gram recall against reference summaries), ROUGE-L (longest-common-subsequence F-measure), ROUGE-W (weighted LCS) and ROUGE-S/SU (skip-bigram co-occurrence, optionally with unigrams) (pp. 1-5). Seventeen variants are validated by correlating systems' average ROUGE scores with human content-coverage scores on DUC 2001-2003 single-document, very-short and multi-document summarisation data, with bootstrap 95% intervals (pp. 5-7). ROUGE-2, -L, -W and -S work well for single-document summaries, while correlations in the high 90s were hard to reach for multi-document summaries (p. 7).
size: 17 ROUGE measures (ROUGE-N for N = 1 to 9, ROUGE-L, ROUGE-W, and ROUGE-S and ROUGE-SU at three skip distances) tested on DUC 2001-2003: single-document 100-word summaries from 12 (2001) and 14 (2002) systems, very short summaries from 14 systems (2003), and multi-document summaries of 10 to 400 words from 6 to 18 systems (pp. 5-6).
source_of_items: DUC 2001, 2002 and 2003 system summaries, manual reference summaries and human coverage judgements (pp. 5-6)
evaluation: expression-level metric (n-gram, LCS and skip-bigram overlap with references); the metric is evaluated by Pearson correlation (Spearman and Kendall said to track it) between system-level ROUGE and human coverage scores (p. 6)
human_validation: No new human judgements: the paper uses DUC's human content-coverage scores, assigned with the SEE tool against one manual summary (p. 6).

engtrace_use.sentence: We employ BERTScore (Zhang et al., 2020) to measure deep semantic similarity via contextual embedding alignment, and ROUGE-2 (Lin, 2004) to quantify lexical overlap. (Section 4.3, L468-472)
engtrace_use.explanation: For ROUGE the clause is right: ROUGE-N is n-gram co-occurrence recall between a candidate and reference summaries (p. 1, Eq. 1), so ROUGE-2 measures bigram, that is lexical, overlap. As with BERTScore, the next sentence is not supported: 'Together, these metrics assess the model's ability to employ appropriate domain-specific terminology' (L472-474). ROUGE was designed and validated for the content coverage of summaries on DUC data (p. 1, pp. 5-7), and Lin's own example gives 'police kill the gunman' and 'the gunman kill police' the same ROUGE-2 score against 'police killed the gunman' despite their very different meanings (p. 3). The May paper also reports ROUGE-L (results table header, L633; L604) and uses 'ROUGE-L / BERTScore' in Table 12, but S-V3 introduces only ROUGE-2.

suggested_wording: Lexical-overlap metrics such as ROUGE (Lin, 2004), which counts the n-grams and subsequences a text shares with human reference summaries and was validated against human coverage judgements of summaries, do not track meaning: Lin's own example gives two sentences of very different meaning the same ROUGE-2 score.
facts_to_cite: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) scores a summary by counting units, such as n-grams, word sequences and word pairs, that it shares with human reference summaries (p. 1).
ROUGE-N is n-gram recall against the references (p. 1, Eq. 1); ROUGE-L is an F-measure on the longest common subsequence (p. 2).
Seventeen ROUGE variants were validated by correlating systems' average scores with human content-coverage scores on DUC 2001-2003, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (pp. 5-6).

ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, ROUGE-W and ROUGE-S worked well for single-document summaries; ROUGE-N with N > 1 did significantly worse than the other measures on very short summaries; for multi-document summaries correlations in the high 90s were hard to reach (p. 7).
Lin's example: against 'police killed the gunman', the sentences 'police kill the gunman' and 'the gunman kill police' receive the same ROUGE-2 score although their meanings differ (p. 3).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares only reference-based comparison of generated text with a human reference. Lacks: any check of values, units or reasoning; step-level evaluation; generated instances; gold traces; the engineering domain; and expert validation (its validation is system-level correlation with DUC coverage scores, p. 6).
